subject.title: [Feature]: Support arbitrary workspace files in bootstrap context injection

question: Should OpenClaw accept explicitly configured custom-basename bootstrap files as a core hook contract, or keep bootstrap-extra-files limited to recognized workspace filenames?
rationale: The request changes deterministic system-prompt context and the set of workspace files the runtime reads automatically, which is a product/security boundary choice rather than a strict bug repair.

options.title: Approve Guarded Custom Files
options.body: Allow custom-basename files through the existing hook path after a rebased PR preserves path containment, budgets, ordering, and session filtering.

options.title: Keep Recognized Basenames
options.body: Keep the current allowlist and close or redirect custom-file requests to first-class filename or workspace-convention proposals.

options.title: Defer To Broader Context API
options.body: Leave arbitrary injection open until maintainers choose a more general context-file API instead of extending this bundled hook.

recommendation.title: Approve Guarded Custom Files
recommendation.body: Allow custom-basename files through the existing hook path after a rebased PR preserves path containment, budgets, ordering, and session filtering.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the best available routing candidate from the merged history for the workspace bootstrap hook and related product boundary.
